red_flags: Hard fixed lump, skin dimpling, or peau d'orange — carcinoma until proven otherwise; urgent surgical referral
Bloody nipple discharge or new nipple retraction
Diffuse red hot breast in a non-lactating woman that does not settle — inflammatory carcinoma can mimic an abscess
Lump with hard axillary or supraclavicular nodes
Eczema of the nipple that does not heal — Paget's disease of the nipple
Hard eccentric lump in a male breast — male carcinoma is easily dismissed as gynecomastia
exam: Inspect both breasts with arms by the sides, raised, and pressing on hips — asymmetry, dimpling, peau d'orange, nipple retraction or scaling
Palpate all four quadrants and the axillary tail of both breasts systematically
Define the lump: site, size, consistency, surface, and margins
Assess mobility — freely mobile ('breast mouse') vs tethered to skin vs fixed to pectoralis (re-test with the muscle contracted)
Test for fluctuation and local warmth — abscess or cyst
Gently express the nipple and note discharge color and whether it comes from one duct or many
Palpate both axillae for nodes — number, consistency, fixity — and the supraclavicular fossae
Record temperature when the breast is inflamed
In men, distinguish a soft symmetric subareolar disc (gynecomastia) from a hard eccentric mass
Examine for hepatomegaly when carcinoma is suspected

investigations.why: First-line under 40 and in lactation: separates a simple cyst (settles the diagnosis) from a solid lump (fibroadenoma vs carcinoma) and shows an abscess cavity
First-line over 40 or with any suspicious exam finding: spiculated mass and clustered microcalcification support carcinoma; also screens the contralateral breast
Third arm of triple assessment — the tissue answer separating fibroadenoma, cyst contents, fat necrosis, and carcinoma; core biopsy preferred when carcinoma is suspected
Leukocytosis with high CRP supports abscess/mastitis; both normal in fibroadenoma, cyst, and most carcinomas
Recurrent non-lactational breast sepsis and periductal mastitis are commoner with diabetes and smoking
Excludes chronic liver disease and endocrine causes behind true gynecomastia before labeling it drug-related
